metadata.title: Larotrectinib Monotherapy – Adult
metadata.indication: Adult NTRK gene-fusion-positive locally advanced or metastatic solid tumour, or tumour where resection is likely to cause severe morbidity, with no satisfactory treatment option.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

contexts.duration_text: Continuous until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable rule and confirm all dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00758 Version 3. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: Adult NTRK gene-fusion-positive locally advanced or metastatic solid tumour, or tumour where surgery is likely to cause severe morbidity, with no satisfactory treatment option.

treatment.schedule_summary: Larotrectinib 100 mg orally twice daily continuously
treatment.duration_text: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

ntrk_fusion_confirmed.label: NTRK gene fusion confirmed by a validated test method

hypersensitivity.label: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component

active_uncontrolled_infection.label: Active uncontrolled systemic bacterial, viral or fungal infection

strong_moderate_cyp3a4_pgp_inducer.label: Strong or moderate CYP3A4/P-gp inducer co-administered

major_surgery_within_2_weeks.label: Major surgery within 2 weeks before cycle 1 day 1

other_toxicity_grade.label: Other larotrectinib-related adverse-reaction grade
other_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the named adverse event and apply the toxicity-specific CTCAE definition; assess symptoms, intervention and functional impact.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild or asymptomatic; observation only and intervention generally not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; local or non-invasive intervention may be indicated; may limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

toxicity_not_resolved_within_4_weeks.label: Grade 3–4 adverse reaction has not resolved within 4 weeks

three_dose_modifications_not_tolerated.label: Unable to tolerate larotrectinib after three dose modifications

alt_ast_uln_multiple.label: Highest ALT or AST multiple of ULN

grade4_lft_after_resumption.label: Grade 4 ALT/AST elevation occurred after resuming treatment

hepatic_recurrence_after_resumption.label: Severe hepatic adverse reaction recurred after resuming treatment

action.message: If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, reduce larotrectinib by 50% and resume the prior dose after 3–5 inhibitor half-lives.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

action.message: Grade 3–4 non-hepatic adverse reactions require withholding until baseline or Grade 1, then resumption at the next dose modification if recovery occurs within 4 weeks.

rules.explanation: Grade 3–4 non-hepatic adverse reactions require withholding until baseline or Grade 1, then resumption at the next dose modification if recovery occurs within 4 weeks.

action.message: Permanently discontinue if a Grade 3–4 adverse reaction does not resolve within 4 weeks.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue if a Grade 3–4 adverse reaction does not resolve within 4 weeks.

action.message: Permanently discontinue if larotrectinib cannot be tolerated after three dose modifications.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue if larotrectinib cannot be tolerated after three dose modifications.

action.message: Reduce the starting larotrectinib dose by 50% for Child-Pugh B or C hepatic impairment.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: Reduce the starting larotrectinib dose by 50% for Child-Pugh B or C hepatic impairment.

action.message: ALT/AST above 3 and up to 5 ×ULN requires frequent serial laboratory evaluation and review for interruption or reduction.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: ALT/AST above 3 and up to 5 ×ULN requires frequent serial laboratory evaluation and review for interruption or reduction.

action.message: ALT/AST above 5 ×ULN with bilirubin below 2 ×ULN requires withholding and frequent monitoring; resume at the next dose modification only after recovery and benefit–risk review.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: ALT/AST above 5 ×ULN with bilirubin below 2 ×ULN requires withholding and frequent monitoring; resume at the next dose modification only after recovery and benefit–risk review.

action.message: ALT/AST at least 3 ×ULN with bilirubin at least 2 ×ULN requires withholding, frequent monitoring and consideration of permanent discontinuation.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: ALT/AST at least 3 ×ULN with bilirubin at least 2 ×ULN requires withholding, frequent monitoring and consideration of permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Permanently discontinue for Grade 4 ALT/AST elevation after treatment resumption.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue for Grade 4 ALT/AST elevation after treatment resumption.

action.message: Permanently discontinue if the severe hepatic adverse reaction recurs after resuming treatment.

source.document: Official NCCP regimen; source-specific decision pathway

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue if the severe hepatic adverse reaction recurs after resuming treatment.
